caption: Two homes, one marriage. What's the cost of distance in your household?

slides.title:
How we spend our
R42 000 household
income across two towns
South Africa
Living in Vryburg
slides.body:
Him 38, her 36
Married, two kids (8 and 5)
Jobs: Mine electrician in Hotazel (away Mon–Thu) & Home Affairs clerk
Household net income: R42 000 p/m

slides.title: Bond repayment
slides.includes: 3 bed in Vryburg, rates and water
slides.body: He's home three nights a week. The kids still ask if he lives here.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Two kitchens: ours, and his in Hotazel
slides.body: He buys his own food there. We don't talk about how much of it is takeaways.

slides.title: School fees & aftercare
slides.includes: Private primary and aftercare until five
slides.body: I work till half past four, so aftercare is the thing that makes my job possible.

slides.title: Fuel for the trip
slides.includes: His Sunday night drive and the monthly family visit
slides.body: Two hundred and eighty kilometres each way. I did the sum once and then stopped.

slides.title: His room in Hotazel
slides.includes: Shared house, own room, rent only
slides.body: A second rent just so he can work. Neither of us thought of it when we got married.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Car instalments, medical aid, electricity, phones, funeral policies, stokvel
slides.body: Two car instalments, because one of them lives on the road.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R42 000. We're not struggling, but there's R2 800 that exists only because of the distance.

slides.title: I stopped guessing
slides.body:
I uploaded both our statements to Beyond Horizon and the two kitchens finally showed up as one grocery number.

The second rent was easy to forget.

No bank login needed.
